youtube_title: Seul Choix Point Lighthouse: cigar smoke and the keeper who died there in 1910
body: Visitors say they smell cigar smoke at Seul Choix Point Lighthouse, on Lake Michigan near Gulliver in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. The name is French for 'only choice' (locals say 'Sis-shwa'). The tower's light was first lit in 1895 and it still guides ships. In 1910, keeper Joseph Willie Townshend died in the keeper's house, and accounts say he lay in state in the parlor until his family could gather. Since then, volunteers and guests have reported the smell of his cigars, silverware moved on the table and a man's face in a mirror. The president of the Gulliver Historical Society says she has written more than 150 true stories from guests and volunteers. The lighthouse is a museum, open from Memorial Day weekend through September. 👻 Comment your town, and it could be next! #SeulChoix #Gulliver #UpperPeninsula #Michigan #Lighthouse #Haunted #LaPorteAfterDark
